title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: on the previous page Grothendieck defines, by induction on card I, a 'donnée de conicité' (conic structure) on a datum (X, (X_i)_{i in I}, (B_alpha, xi_alpha)_{alpha in Lambda}). Here X is a space stratified by closed subspaces X_i indexed by a finite poset I. The (B_alpha, xi_alpha) form a transversal family of 'cylindrical' boundary subspaces with collar data. The induction runs as follows. Let I_0 be the set of minimal elements of I. Choose a strict conic neighbourhood (tube) T_{I_0} of X_{I_0} = union of X_beta, beta in I_0, transversal to the B_alpha and hence to the X_i. Removing the open tube gives a new space X*, stratified by I* = I \ I_0. Its family of cylindrical boundaries is enlarged by the tube boundaries (dot X_beta, xi_beta). Each X_beta carries the induced boundary data B_{beta alpha}. One then requires recursively a conic structure on this new datum. This is a combinatorial-topological version of Thom-Mather control data, organised as a 'deployment' (unfolding) of the stratified space into a manifold-with-corners-like object.

This page lists three remarks.
(1) Existence and equisingularity. Under suitable non-degeneracy hypotheses on the initial datum, a conic structure should exist. If the stratification is equisingular along the open strata X_i^0 := X_i \ union_{j<i} X_j, there should exist an equisingular conic structure (with the obvious ad hoc definition). By the induction, it suffices to construct an equisingular tube around the union X_{I_0} of the minimal strata.
(2) Choice of filtration. More generally, take any strictly increasing chain 0 ⊂ I_0 ⊂ I_1 ⊂ ... ⊂ I_n = I such that each I_i \ I_{i-1} consists of minimal elements of I \ I_{i-1}. One can then define recursively a notion of conic structure adapted to this 'filtration': peel off a whole layer of minimal strata at each step. The canonical choice is I_0 = all minimal elements, and so on. He states the expectation, or claim, that the notion is essentially independent of the filtration chosen.
(3) Generalising the boundary data. Instead of a family (B_alpha, xi_alpha), one may give on X a 'cylindrical stratification of type Lambda'. This is equivalent to the family case when the cylindrical stratification is modelled on |S(Lambda)|^0, presumably the open realisation of the simplex/poset of subsets of Lambda, i.e. a corner model. The next page says this makes no essential difference and announces a later localisation ('stratification cylindrique locale') and §9 on 'stratification cônique de type I'.

Purpose: to set up an intrinsic, inductive theory of conic or tubular structures on stratified spaces, compatible with corners, as a step toward the 'déploiement' of stratified spaces of the Esquisse d'un programme.
errors: No outright errors, but the remarks are heuristic ('il doit être vrai'). 'Non-dégénérescence' is not defined; in the real/analytic setting one needs something like Whitney (b) or Thom-Mather conditions. Mere equisingularity along strata is not obviously enough to guarantee an equisingular tube without further regularity.
Remark 2's independence claim is stated without proof. The meaning of 'essentiellement' is unspecified (presumably up to a contractible or canonical choice, or isotopy).

ideas.what: Inductive definition of conic structure by peeling off tubes around minimal strata, with tube boundaries adjoined as new cylindrical boundary pieces (corners)
ideas.modern_name: Thom-Mather control data / systems of tubes; resolution or unfolding of stratified spaces into manifolds with (fibred) corners
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom (1969), Mather (1970/1973); Verona (1984, 'Stratified mappings'); Brasselet-Hector-Saralegi (unfolding); Albin-Leichtnam-Mazzeo-Piazza and Melrose (resolution to manifolds with fibred corners)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), sections on tame topology and the 'dévissage' of stratified structures, sketched there without details

ideas.what: Existence of conic structure under non-degeneracy; equisingular conic structure reduces to building an equisingular tube around the minimal strata
ideas.modern_name: Existence of control data for Whitney stratifications; Thom-Mather first isotopy lemma
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mather, Thom; Lojasiewicz/Whitney for regularity conditions

ideas.what: Conic structures relative to arbitrary 'layer' filtrations of the index poset (successive antichains of minimal elements), and expected independence of the choice
ideas.modern_name: Independence of the order of blowing up / resolving strata; contractibility of the space of control data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in control-data theory; for resolutions, Albin-Melrose et al. (iterated blow-up in any compatible order)

ideas.what: Replacing a family of collared boundary pieces by a 'cylindrical stratification of type Lambda' modelled on |S(Lambda)|^0
ideas.modern_name: Manifolds with corners / <n>-manifolds (Jänich, Laures); corner structures indexed by posets

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates, but does not prove here, the independence of the inductive notion of conic structure from the chosen filtration of the stratification poset by layers of minimal elements. In modern terms this is a coherence statement: the categories or spaces of conic structures for different admissible filtrations should be canonically equivalent.
missed.quote: on pourrait définir par récurrence une notion de structure cônique pour cette "filtration" de I. Mais on peut [s'attendre/montrer] que cette notion ne dépend pas en fait, essentiellement, de la filtration choisie.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Analogous independence-of-order results exist for iterated blow-ups to manifolds with fibred corners. A clean statement at the level of control data or exit-path infinity-categories is rarely made explicit, but this is likely folklore and of minor novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard-type remarks within Grothendieck's private development of tubular/conic structures, which parallels Thom-Mather control data and later resolution-to-corners theories. The filtration-independence question is a nice but folklore-level point. Nothing seems absent from the literature in substance.
transcription_corrections: The collar data should read xi_alpha (as on the previous page), not script E_alpha.
In the definition of X_i^0, the subscript under the union is written 'j<i' with 'j≤i' also visible beneath; the intended reading is X_i \ union_{j<i} X_j.
'Mais on peut se demander que cette notion ne dépend pas' is likely 'Mais on peut s'attendre (or: montrer) que cette notion ne dépend pas, en fait, essentiellement, de la filtration choisie'.
Remark 1 ends 'il suffit de pouvoir construire un tube équisingulier autour de X_{I_0} ...'.

The insertion above 'cylindriques' in remark 3 reads 'de type', i.e. 'stratification cylindrique de type [Lambda]'; the last line reads roughly 'lorsqu'on se donne que des stratifications cylindriques sur |S(Lambda)|^0'.
